card_title: My boyfriend said he flew to Italy. The flight tracker said that flight never existed.
title: My boyfriend said he flew to Italy. The flight tracker said otherwise.
lines: My boyfriend said he flew to Italy. The flight tracker said that flight never existed.
We'd been together three months. I drove him to the airport myself. He said he was visiting family.
At one twenty, he called me from the boarding line.
At two, he texted: taking off.
I picked up his dog. I was pet-sitting while he was away.
And here's the thing. Flying makes me anxious. Even when I'm not the one on the plane.
So I opened a flight tracker. I just wanted to watch his plane cross the map.
There was no flight to Italy.
Not at that time. Not from my airport.
I told myself I was reading it wrong.
At four fifteen, he texted: landed.
Later, the story changed.
Now his flight had been going to Ibiza. It got canceled. And they diverted him to Brindisi.
So I checked the Brindisi airport website.
No matching arrival.
But two flights did leave my airport right at his time.
One to Reus, in Spain. One to Nice, in France.
When I asked him about it, suddenly he was rushing for a train. Bad reception. Talk later.
I sat there with his dog, and a map full of planes that weren't his.
Eventually, he admitted it. He flew to Nice.
First, he said he took a train down to Calabria.
Then he said he was in Liguria.
Three different stories.
I still don't know why he went. And honestly, I've stopped needing to know.
I ended it. I told him to stop contacting me.
He found someone else to pick him up from the airport.
And his dog and his car? They're going back to him. With someone standing right next to me.
Three months. One flight tracker. That's all it took.
